answer: Because the pearl index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the gale audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 95 aliases therefore needs 95 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a karst index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
